subject: Concept art of a sci-fi strategy game's colony screen: a small frontier colony on the rocky, airless surface of a moon of a gas giant, seen from above at about 45 degrees. Five buildings of one family (modular and industrial, steel-gray plated walls, dark slate frames, thin electric-blue light strips and windows), each on its own flat octagonal foundation pad, spaced neatly apart across the middle of the picture and linked by thin paths: a metal mine with a lattice drill tower over a shaft, a helium-3 extractor with a tall mast and spherical tanks, a chip fab (a long, low clean-room hall with radiator fins on its roof), a depot of stacked cargo containers under a gantry crane, and the command center, the tallest, a tower with a sensor dish and a small launch pad. The ground: gray rock and fine dust, a few small craters and low ridges. The horizon runs across the upper part of the picture; above it a huge banded gas giant in pale blue and slate rises big in the black sky, lit from one side by a distant sun, with pin-sharp stars. The lower third of the picture is open, flat, calm ground with nothing on it, left free for interface cards. No vehicles, no people.
style: Minimal, calm and neat, with a lot of empty dark space. Palette: space and dark surfaces in deep navy blacks (#0A0F16, #111722, #192130) and slate blues (#242D41, #3E4D6B); light in electric blue to pale cyan (#4E87BB, #71B2D8, #ACDBE9), the only bright accent; hulls in cool steel grays (#686A79, #97999F). Crisp and sharp everywhere: clean hard edges, fine detail, pin-sharp stars; no haze, no soft focus, no depth-of-field or motion blur. Realistic light, cinematic concept art. No text, no logos, no interface, no lens flares.
